To merge the last two commits in Git, you can use an interactive rebase. Here are the main methods:

## Method 1: Using Interactive Rebase

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

This will open your default text editor with something like:
```
pick abc1234 Second to last commit
pick def5678 Last commit
```

Change `pick` to `squash` (or `s`) for the last commit:
```
pick abc1234 Second to last commit
squash def5678 Last commit
```

Save and close the editor. Git will then open another editor to combine the commit messages.

## Method 2: Using Reset and Commit

```bash
# Soft reset to 2 commits ago (keeps changes staged)
git reset --soft HEAD~2

# Create a new commit with all the changes
git commit -m "Your new commit message"
```

## Method 3: Using Fixup (if you don't need the last commit message)

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

Change the second commit from `pick` to `fixup` (or `f`):
```
pick abc1234 Second to last commit
fixup def5678 Last commit
```

This will merge the commits and discard the last commit's message.

## Important Notes:
- ⚠️ Only do this if you haven't pushed these commits yet
- If you've already pushed, you'll need to force push after rebasing: `git push --force-with-lease`
- This rewrites history, so coordinate with your team if working on a shared branch
